name: What is a bump-out addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out addition is a micro-extension that expands an existing room outward by roughly two to ten feet without building a full-scale room addition. Rather than creating an entirely new standalone space, a bump-out enhances the footprint of a room you already use. Homeowners commonly use bump-outs to create space for a kitchen island, insert a dining nook, fit a double vanity or soaking tub in a bathroom, or add a walk-in closet to a bedroom. This approach gives you the exact square footage needed for functional layout improvements without consuming substantial yard space or requiring the broader structural support of an entire room build.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out addition is a small-scale home extension extending 2 to 10 feet outward to enlarge an existing room, such as adding space for a kitchen island or a larger bathroom vanity.
